doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Choosing instruments for Garden of Redemption's end credits
summary: He composes with specific instruments in mind, such as the English horn, rather than orchestrating afterward.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Here’s a very specific question: I think you did the music for “Garden of Redemption”?
And on the end credits there’s this very moving piece of music that probably is as the credits scroll, and you had the melody and I think it was an English horn. Do you recall that?
Yeah. And then it was passed to the cello. I don’t really have a question except it’s an observation that it was beautifully done and did you choose the English horn for a particular reason?

Yes is the answer. A very simple answer. I think interestingly, and this is possibly something that doesn’t get picked up a lot, as someone who orchestrates and generally orchestrates my own compositions, I always compose thinking of particular sounds or instruments. So to pick a trumpet or an English horn or a French horn or whatever it

might be is always a deliberate thing in the composition process, not even when — so when I orchestrate I actually know what I’m going to be writing rather than oh I wonder what instrument that would sound good on. It’s slightly different I think from a lot of composers who would just write something and then oh what can I put this on.
Yeah because then you’re running into like that doesn’t lie very well on this instrument now I’ve got to fuss with it.
